gvc_ranger.text: Glenveagh is one of Ireland's six national parks. Mountains, lakes, bog, woodland and the castle, all looked after for everybody.
The bog is the bit people overlook. It's thousands of years deep, it holds more carbon than a forest, and it's full of sundews, which eat flies. Small, sticky, terrifying. If you're a fly.

gvc_child.text: We saw a golden eagle! Well, Miss said it was a golden eagle. Ciara says it was a crow. Ciara is wrong about everything.
